extracted.intended_audience: Members of the ALSC Newbery Medal selection committee (ALSC award committee members and Chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, definitions, eligibility rules, evaluative criteria, and committee conduct guidelines for selecting the John Newbery Medal (the most distinguished contribution to American literature for children) for a given publication year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal award terms (annual; most distinguished contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the author of the most distinguished contribution to American literature for children published by an American publisher in the United States in English during the preceding year; honor books may be named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee function is to select the most distinguished contribution to American literature for children from books published in English in the preceding year within the terms, definitions, and criteria governing the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility: citizenship or residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal is restricted to authors who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of 'resident' and 'citizen' clarify edge cases (green card holders, living in U.S. at least six months/year, temporary absence while maintaining permanent U.S. home). The Chair/PGC may be consulted for uncertain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider only eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee's decision is to be made following deliberation about books of the specified calendar year; do not consider an author's entire body of work or prior awards when evaluating eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'contribution to American literature' (text-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Contribution to American literature' indicates the text of a book and implies consideration of all forms of writing—fiction, non-fiction, and poetry. Reprints, compilations, and abridgements are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary focus is on textual contribution; other book components may be considered only when they make the book less effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'contribution to American literature for children' (intended audience up to 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: A book for which children are an intended potential audience (up to and including age 14). The book should display respect for children's understandings, abilities, and appreciations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books for the entire age range are to be considered; committee should ask whether there is any 14‑year‑old for whom the book is suitable and whether it is distinguished for that audience. A book appealing to a narrow part of the range may still be eligible if exceptionally distinguished for that readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'distinguished'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Distinguished' is defined as marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement; marked by excellence in quality; conspicuous excellence or eminence; individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the central evaluative standard for selecting winners and honor books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'original work' (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original work means the text was created by this writer and no one else (may include original retellings provided words are author's own); it is presented for the first time and was not previously published elsewhere in any form. Text reprinted or compiled from other sources and abridgements are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that previously published texts or compiled material generally are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and publication location requirements ('In English' and 'American literature published in the United States')
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In English' means the committee considers only books written and published in English (use of other-language words/phrases allowed where appropriate). 'American literature published in the United States' means books first published in other countries are not eligible; simultaneously published books may be eligible; U.S. territories and commonwealths are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a book was first published abroad, it is not eligible even if author is resident in U.S.; exceptions and edge cases should be discussed with PGC/Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication year requirement ('Published during the preceding year')
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must have a publication date in the year under consideration, be available for purchase in that year, and have a copyright date no later than that year. Books should be eligible only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book with an earlier copyright but not published until the year under consideration is eligible for the later year; if published prior to its copyright year, consider the year of copyright stated in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluative elements (literary dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In identifying 'distinguished contribution to American literature,' committee members need to consider: interpretation of the theme or concept; presentation of information (including accuracy, clarity, and organization); development of a plot; delineation of characters; delineation of a setting; appropriateness of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because literary qualities vary by content, committees need not expect excellence in every listed element; the book should have distinguished qualities in the elements pertinent to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of theme or concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how the author interprets and handles the book's theme or central concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider depth, originality, clarity of thematic exploration and how it serves a child audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of information (accuracy, clarity, organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: For informational/nonfiction works, presentation includes accuracy of content, clarity of exposition, and logical organization of material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider author authority, currency of information, documentation, and whether presentation stimulates understanding and curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plot structure, pacing, coherence, and how effectively events are developed to serve the book's aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider suitability for intended child readership and whether plot development contributes to literary distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of character development, individuality, depth, and believability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether characters are appropriately developed for the book's form and audience and contribute to its distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how setting is rendered and how it supports the narrative or informational goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider specificity, appropriateness, and evocative quality for child readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of style
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book's language, voice, tone, and stylistic choices are appropriate for the content and child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style should contribute to the book's excellence and suitability for children up to age 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of presentation for a child audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must consider excellence of presentation specifically for children (respectful, clear, engaging).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation includes the textual presentation and may include features that affect comprehension and engagement for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-weighting: decision primarily on the text
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book is to be considered as a contribution to American literature; the committee is to make its decision primarily on the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other components (illustrations, overall design, extras) may be considered only when they make the book less effective; the award is for literary quality and quality presentation for children, not for illustrations per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained entity requirement (not dependent on other media)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (sound or film equipment) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supplemental media are included (CD, website), only the book itself is considered for the award; citations should note that supporting media were not part of the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose: literary quality over didacticism or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is for literary quality and quality presentation for children; it is not for didactic content or popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should avoid conflating moral/instructional aims or sales/popularity with literary distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and representation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusiveness is a core value: books should demonstrate integrity and respect for all children’s lives and experiences and should not diminish or denigrate any individual or group through stereotypes, whitewashing, or derogatory content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works with consideration of all children rather than privileging dominant culture; while works do not have to include diverse characters, they should not disrespect diverse lives or histories. Committee members are encouraged to be aware of their own perspectives and biases and to seek learning when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee conduct: ALSC Community Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for meeting behavior: speak for yourself, embrace multiple perspectives (dialogue not debate), be aware of privilege/oppression, use correct pronouns, share the air, interrupt derailment, acknowledge intent vs. impact, interrupt bias and accept feedback, and remember growth opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these agreements to guide respectful, equitable discussion; add additional group agreements as needed; 'ouch'/'oops' may be used to mark problematic moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest: definition and general policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A conflict of interest occurs when an individual's personal or private interests may lead a reasonable observer to question whether professional actions or decisions are influenced by considerations of significant personal or private interest (financial or otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must avoid conflicts and even appearance of conflicts; when in doubt, consult ALSC Executive Director prior to accepting appointment; situations arising during service should be directed to ALSC leadership; final decision rests with the Executive Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific conflict prohibitions (authors/illustrators; publishers; close relationships; financial stake)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members who have written or illustrated a book eligible during their term should not accept appointment; members may not be employed by a children's trade-book publisher/author/illustrator beyond assigned library duties; do not accept appointment if close family or personal relationships with eligible authors/illustrators or with persons employed by U.S. trade publishers; do not accept appointment if you or close family directly own equity >5% in a U.S. trade publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are disqualifying relationships intended to protect the integrity of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and external communication restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must maintain a high degree of confidentiality regarding committee discussions (oral and written, in-person and virtual). Members may express only their own opinions and may not quote or indicate which titles are under consideration outside the committee. Members must not engage in print or electronic communication about eligible titles during their term (professional journals, blogs, social media, signed reviews, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are encouraged to obtain critical opinions from others but must avoid implying a book is 'under consideration' (only Chair may approach outside readers and may only tell them a book is 'eligible'). Mock elections are prohibited. Violations may result in dismissal and preclusion from future service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for relationship with publishers (committee side)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may accept unsolicited eligible books from publishers; the Chair compiles a roster for publishers and surveys members on missing titles; members are not to solicit publishers for free personal copies; avoid conflicts arising from personal contact with publishing personnel; unsolicited offers (invitations/favors) may be accepted only if they do not influence book consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair/PGC may contact publishers to obtain difficult-to-find titles; members bear responsibility for obtaining books and should follow Chair guidance when unable to obtain a title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for publishers submitting books
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should review award terms and criteria and submit one copy of the work to the award committee Chair (optionally send to each committee member). A list of committee members is available via the award Terms and Criteria page. Submission deadline is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers are encouraged to support the committee's work but must follow submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of self-published and small-press titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-published and small-press books are eligible provided they meet all other eligibility requirements. They are eligible in their first year only; if later republished by another publisher, they will not be reconsidered upon commercial publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair keeps a list of eligible self-published/small-press titles received directly; sharing with committee is at Chair's discretion, often with committee input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format eligibility: 'Book' vs e-book
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Book' means the work was published in book format (pages between covers). Electronic-only books (e-books) and technological additions (CDs, DVDs, accompanying websites) are excluded from consideration of the book itself. A book first published as an e-book and later as hardcover/paperback is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supplementary media are included, only the book itself is considered; award citations should note that supporting media were not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting attendance and access to materials requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons appointed should be able to attend all required discussion and decision meetings (virtual and in-person) scheduled for the year, including mandatory in-person LibLearnX final selection meeting, and have ready access to the major part of the current output of children's books through libraries, bookstores, and interlibrary loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a committee member cannot obtain certain titles, arrangements for review copies may be made as prescribed in committee guidelines; full participation is required for wise selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of service limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may serve on certain ALSC award committees (Newbery, Caldecott, etc.) more often than once every four years (counting from last year of term). This rule does not apply to Chairs or in emergency mid-year replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations may result in dismissal and preclusion from future award committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's book age-suitability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a book's suitability across the 0–14 range is in question, committees should consider whether any 14‑year‑old would find it suitable, whether it is distinguished enough to be universally known, whether it deserves recognition for excellence for a narrow readership, or whether it is exceptionally fine for the age segment it targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should answer: Is there any 14‑year‑old for whom this book is suitable? If so, is it distinguished enough to be considered? If so, exactly which 14‑year‑olds would respond and why?

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative checklist / note-taking criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested note-taking/evaluation items include: Title/Author/Illustrator; whether you suggested/nominated it; Subject/Summary; Quality of Writing (excellent, engaging, distinctive language); Child Audience (respect for children's understanding up to age 14); for informational books—accuracy, organization, documentation, clarity, stimulating presentation, features (index, TOC, bibliography, glossary, graphics, author note).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reminder: Not every book relies equally on every element. The committee need not find excellence across the board, but rather in elements relevant to the book. The book must be self-contained.
